questions.stem_latex:
A number of fish species are subject to minimum length regulations when they are caught.

ie. fish shorter than a given length must be returned to the water if caught.

Two such species are Red Snapper and Barramundi which have minimum lengths of 30 cm and 55 cm respectively.

A fishing tour operator in Northern Australia has made observations over a long period of time and found that, when measured in cm, both the variables ‘R’ (the lengths of caught Red Snapper) and ‘B’ (the lengths of caught Barramundi), are normally distributed.

‘R’ has a mean of 36 cm and standard deviation of 3 cm. ‘B’ has a standard deviation of 4 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.latex: Calculate the mean length of Barramundi caught if $2.5\%$ of Barramundi caught are less than 54 cm.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: Calculate the $z$-scores for the minimum allowed lengths for both variables, R and B, and comment upon what this means in terms of which of the two species are more likely to be returned to the water after capture.

As part of the selection process for an available job, an employer requires candidates to complete the test faster than $90\%$ of all applicants to progress to the next stage.

An extract from a probability table for the standard normal distribution is shown below.

\exfigure{1307_q16d_1}

Darcy completed the aptitude test in 4 minutes and 23 seconds.

Did Darcy qualify for the next stage of selection? Justify your answer by demonstrating your knowledge of the normal distribution and the application of $z$-scores to the problem.

solutions.question: 11(c)
solutions.latex: Total perimeter: $4x+2\pi r=6$, so $2\pi r=6-4x$, $r=\dfrac{6-4x}{2\pi}=\dfrac{3-2x}{\pi}$.

solutions.question: 11(c)
solutions.latex:
Total area $A=\pi r^2+x^2=\pi\left(\dfrac{3-2x}{\pi}\right)^2+x^2=\dfrac{(3-2x)^2}{\pi}+x^2$

$\dfrac{dA}{dx}=\dfrac{1}{\pi}\,2(3-2x)(-2)+2x=\dfrac{-12+8x+2\pi x}{\pi}$

$\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=\dfrac{8+2\pi}{\pi}>0\Rightarrow$ minimum.

Minimum area occurs when $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=0$: $-12+8x+2\pi x=0$, $x(8+2\pi)=12$, $x=\dfrac{12}{8+2\pi}=\dfrac{6}{4+\pi}$.

Length required for the square is $4\times\dfrac{6}{4+\pi}=\dfrac{24}{4+\pi}$.

Length required for the circle is $6-\dfrac{24}{4+\pi}=\dfrac{6\pi}{4+\pi}$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: correct solution; 1: correct finding of area; 1: showing minimum area; 1: correct value of $x$; 1: correct length of square and circle; 1: some progress

solutions.question: 14(d)

$\dfrac{dx}{dt}=-e^{-t}-\dfrac12e^{-2t}+c_1$

Initial conditions: $-\dfrac32=-e^0-\dfrac12e^0+c_1\ \to\ c_1=0$

$\therefore\ x=e^{-t}+\dfrac14e^{-2t}-\dfrac12$ as required.

solutions.question: 16(a)
solutions.latex:
For the domain $0\le x\le6$, $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\right)\ge0$ (shown graphically), hence $f(x)\ge0$.

\exfigure{1307_q16a_s1}

Also,

$\displaystyle\int_0^6\dfrac{\pi}{12}\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\right)dx=\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left[-\dfrac6\pi\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\right)\right]_0^6=\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left[-\dfrac6\pi\cos\pi+\dfrac6\pi\cos0\right]=\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left(-\dfrac6\pi\times-1+\dfrac6\pi\times1\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{12}\times\dfrac{12}{\pi}=1$

$\therefore$ The function is a probability density function since $f(x)\ge0$ and $\displaystyle\int_a^bf(x)\,dx=1$.

solutions.latex: $P(X\le4)=\displaystyle\int_0^4\dfrac{\pi}{12}\sin\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\,dx=\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left[-\dfrac6\pi\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{6}\right]_0^4=\dfrac{\pi}{12}\left(-\dfrac6\pi\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{3}-\left(-\dfrac6\pi\cos0\right)\right)=\dfrac{\pi}{12}\times-\dfrac6\pi\times-\dfrac12+\dfrac{\pi}{12}\times\dfrac6\pi=\dfrac14+\dfrac12=\dfrac34$

solutions.question: 16(c)
solutions.latex:
Using the empirical law, $95\%$ of Barramundi are within 2 standard deviations of the mean, or $5\%$ are more than 2 standard deviations smaller or larger than the mean. Given the symmetry of the normal distribution, $2.5\%$ of Barramundi are smaller than 2 standard deviations less than the mean.

Hence, $54=\mu-2s$, $\ \mu=54+2\times4=62$ cm.

ie. the mean length of caught Barramundi was 62 cm.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 2: correct solution; 1: substantial progress towards correct solution, showing some knowledge of the empirical law

solutions.question: 16(c)
solutions.latex:
R minimum length $=30$ cm: $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{s}=\dfrac{30-36}{3}=-2$

B minimum length $=55$ cm: $z=\dfrac{x-\mu}{s}=\dfrac{55-62}{4}=-1.75$

From the $z$-scores and empirical law, only $2.5\%$ of caught Red Snapper will be returned to the water because they are too small (minimum length is 2 standard deviations from the mean), however, more than $2.5\%$ of Barramundi will be returned to the water as minimum length is only 1.75 standard deviations from the mean. ie. caught Barramundi are more likely to be returned to the water.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution showing z-scores for both species and correct and logical reasoning as to which species is more likely to be thrown back; 2: two of the three elements correct (reasoning based on a single incorrect z-score is acceptable); 1: one of the three elements correct (correct reasoning based upon incorrect z-scores is acceptable)

solutions.question: 16(d)
solutions.latex:
From the table, the $z$-score for an applicant that is faster than $89.97\%$ of the other applicants is $1.28$. The $z$-score of an applicant that is faster than $90.15\%$ of the other applicants is $1.29$.

This means the qualifying time for the next stage would be:

$x=\mu-1.28s=5\text{ minutes}-1.28\times30\text{ seconds}=4\text{ minutes }21.6\text{ seconds}$

OR $x=\mu-1.29s=5\text{ minutes}-1.29\times30\text{ seconds}=4\text{ minutes }21.3\text{ seconds}$

(Either answer would be acceptable. $1.28$ is closer to $90\%$ probability, $1.29$ ensures probability exceeds $90\%$.)

Darcy's time of 4 minutes 23 seconds does not qualify her for the next stage of selection.

(This could also be justified by calculating Darcy's $z$-score: 37 s faster than the mean gives $z=1.23$, less than the $1.28$ required.)
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: correct solution showing the z-score and time required to progress to next stage and correct conclusion; 2: substantial progress towards a correct solution with one of the above elements incorrect; 1: some progress towards correct solution with one of the elements correct
